what_its_for: Donepezil is used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease, including memory loss, confusion, and thinking problems. It does not cure Alzheimer's disease, but it can help slow down how fast symptoms get worse and may help you think more clearly and remember better.
how_to_take: Take donepezil by mouth, usually once a day in the evening, right before bedtime. You can take it with or without food. If you are taking the regular tablet, swallow it whole with a full glass of water. If you are taking the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve completely before swallowing — do not swallow it whole. Do not crush or chew regular tablets.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose of 5 mg once a day at bedtime. After 4 to 6 weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once a day. For moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease, your doctor may increase the dose to 23 mg once a day after at least 3 months on the 10 mg dose. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember that same day. However, if it is almost time for your next dose or you have missed more than one day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you have missed several days of doses, call your doctor before restarting the medication.
storage: Store donepezil at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking donepezil, as it can make dizziness and drowsiness worse and increase your risk of falling. Be careful when driving, operating machinery, or doing anything that requires alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs like Benadryl (diphenhydramine) or sleep aids, as they may interfere with how donepezil works. Avoid taking aspirin or other anti-inflammatory pain relievers (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without checking with your doctor, as they may increase stomach bleeding risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away; fainting or blacking out; slow or irregular heartbeat; difficulty urinating or pain when urinating; seizures; severe stomach pain; coughing up or vomiting blood; muscle cramps or weakness that is getting worse; difficulty breathing or wheezing; or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice that your symptoms are getting significantly worse.
when_it_works: Donepezil may take several weeks before you notice any improvement. Most people begin to see some benefit after 1 to 3 months of taking the medication. Because Alzheimer's disease gets worse over time, the goal of donepezil is to slow down memory loss and thinking problems rather than to completely restore memory. Even if you do not feel a big difference, the medicine may still be helping to slow the progression of your disease. Keep taking it as prescribed and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the side effects of donepezil, especially dizziness, falls, nausea, and slow heart rate. Use extra caution when standing up to avoid falls. Kidney or liver disease: If you have kidney or liver problems, tell your doctor, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Donepezil is generally not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Heart conditions: If you have a slow heart rate, heart rhythm problems, or a history of fainting, tell your doctor before starting donepezil, as it may affect your heart rate. Stomach problems: If you have a history of stomach ulcers or take medications that can cause stomach bleeding, talk to your doctor, as donepezil may increase this risk.
